## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement SBOM-based attestations and runtime provenance checks, plus how to wire CI gates with Kosign and CycloneDX.

## Key Concepts

- Image provenance, cosign signatures, attestations
- CycloneDX SBOMs, embedded in image annotations

## Code Example

```yaml
name: prod-provenance
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - manifests/prod/**
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: setup cosign
        run: |
          curl -sSfL https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/releases/download/v1.10.0/cosign-linux-amd64 -o cosign
          chmod +x cosign
          sudo mv cosign /usr/local/bin/
      - name: verify images
        run: |
          cosign verify -key cosign.pub registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag
      - name: verify SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cyclone_dx_attest --image registry.example.com/namespace/service:tag --attest
```

- How would you handle attestation revocation and key rotation?
- How to scale SBOM checks across many services and environments?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```


## Verification Steps

**Local verification:**
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type sbom --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Check Rekor transparency log
rekor-cli get --uuid <rekor-uuid>
```

**CI verification:**
```bash
# In CI pipeline before deployment
cosign verify \
  --key pub.key \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/org/ML-platform/.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/main" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical policy-as-code skills and integration of admission controls into CI for a multi-cloud, large-scale platform.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA ConstraintTemplate
- securityContext runAsNonRoot and runAsUser
- privileged and capabilities.drop
- hostPath/hostIPC/hostPID prohibition
- CI validation with kubectl/dry-run and Gatekeeper

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (high-level sketch)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sprivilege
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sPrivilege
  targets:
  - target: AdmissionReview
    rego: |
      package k8sprivilege
      violation["privilege violation"] {
        input.review.object.kind == "Deployment"
      }
```
```yaml
# Failing manifest (hostPath & privileged)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
            runAsNonRoot: false
            runAsUser: 0
            capabilities:
              drop: []
      volumes:
        - name: data
          hostPath:
            path: /tmp
            type: Directory
```
```yaml
# Passing manifest (non-root, restricted caps, no hostPath)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-service
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: example/app:latest
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
            privileged: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
      volumes: []
```

- Run Gatekeeper in CI and verify failing/passing manifests via kubectl apply --dry-run and gatekeeper playbooks.
- Confirm PRs fail on bad manifests and pass on good manifests.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1

  name: service-a
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical DevOps security skills by testing your ability to implement automated security gates that prevent secret leakage and ensure deployment consistency, directly connecting code hygiene to CI/CD workflows.

## Key Concepts
- Secret scanning integration in CI pipelines
- Baseline management for handling false positives
- Comprehensive coverage of manifests and Helm values
- Local development vs CI environment verification
- Image tag approval and enforcement workflows
- Automated security gates in pull request processes

## Code Example

### GitHub Actions CI Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Secret Scan & Image Validation
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
      - '**/values.yaml'
      - '**/Chart.yaml'

jobs:
  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install detect-secrets
        run: pip install detect-secrets

      - name: Scan for secrets
        run: |
          # Initialize baseline if it doesn't exist
          if [ ! -f .secrets.baseline ]; then
            detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline
          fi
          
          # Run scan and fail if new secrets detected
          detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline --all-files
          
          # Check for any high-entropy results
          if detect-secrets audit --report .secrets.baseline | grep -q "High Entropy"; then
            echo "❌ Secrets detected! Please review and remove before merging."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate image tags
        run: |
          # Define approved tags (in production, store this securely)
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest"
          
          # Extract image tags from manifests
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" | \
            sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://' | \
            sort -u > /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          # Validate each tag
          while IFS= read -r tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag '$tag' is not in approved list: $APPROVED_TAGS"
              exit 1
            fi
          done < /tmp/current_tags.txt
          
          echo "✅ All image tags are approved"

      - name: Comment on PR (if failed)
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: '🚨 **Security Scan Failed**\n\nThis PR contains either hardcoded secrets or unapproved image tags. Please review the failed job and fix the issues before merging.'
            })
```

### Example Manifest That Would Fail
```yaml
# deployment-with-secrets.yaml (THIS WOULD FAIL THE SCAN)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: webapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: webapp
        # ❌ Unapproved image tag - will fail validation
        image: myregistry/webapp:v1.3.0-beta
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        env:
        # ❌ Hardcoded secret - will fail scanning
        - name: DATABASE_PASSWORD
          value: "super-secret-password-12345"
        - name: API_KEY
          value: "AKIA1234567890ABCDEFGHI"
        # ❌ Another high-entropy string
        - name: JWT_SECRET
          value: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4gRG9lIiwiaWF0IjoxNTE2MjM5MDIyfQ"
```

### Configuration Files

#### detect-secrets Configuration
```yaml
# .detect-secrets.yml
version: "0.14"
plugins:
  - name: ArtifactoryDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.artifactory
  - name: AWSKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.aws
  - name: Base64HighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "base64"
      min_entropy: 4.5  # Adjust for false positives
  - name: HexHighEntropyString
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.high_entropy_strings
    baseline:
      charset: "hex"
      min_entropy: 3.0
  - name: KeywordDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.keyword
    keyword_exclude: "passkey,password"  # Add safe keywords
  - name: PrivateKeyDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.private_key
  - name: SlackTokenDetector
    path: detect_secrets.plugins.slack

filters:
  - detect_secrets.filters.common.is_likely_id_string
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_indented_comment
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_potential_uuid
  - detect_secrets.filters.heuristic.is_sequential_string

# Paths to exclude from scanning
exclude_files:
  - "tests/.*\.mock\.yaml$"
  - "docs/.*\.md$"
```

#### Pre-commit Hook Configuration
```yaml
# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets
    rev: v1.4.0
    hooks:
      - id: detect-secrets
        args: ['--baseline', '.secrets.baseline']
  
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: validate-image-tags
        name: Validate image tags
        entry: bash -c '
          APPROVED_TAGS="v1.2.0,v1.2.1,latest" &&
          grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" --include="*.yml" |
          sed "s/.*:\s*//" | sed "s/\"//g" | sed "s/.*://" |
          sort -u | while read tag; do
            if [[ "$APPROVED_TAGS" != *"$tag"* ]]; then
              echo "❌ Image tag \"$tag\" is not approved"
              exit 1
            fi
          done'
        language: system
        files: \.(yaml|yml)$
```

## Local Verification Steps

### 1. Install Dependencies
```bash
# Install detect-secrets
pip install detect-secrets

# Install pre-commit hooks
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

### 2. Initial Setup
```bash
# Create initial baseline
find . -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" | xargs detect-secrets scan > .secrets.baseline

# Review and audit the baseline
detect-secrets audit .secrets.baseline
```

### 3. Test the Workflow
```bash
# Test with a problematic file (should fail)
cat > test-bad.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-secret
data:
  password: c3VwZXItc2VjcmV0LXBhc3N3b3JkLTEyMzQ1  # base64 encoded secret
EOF

# Run the scan (should fail)
detect-secrets scan --baseline .secrets.baseline test-bad.yaml

# Clean up
rm test-bad.yaml
```

### 4. Test Image Tag Validation
```bash
# Create deployment with unapproved tag
cat > test-deployment.yaml << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myapp:v2.0.0  # Not in approved list
EOF

# This should fail the image tag validation
grep -r "image:" . --include="*.yaml" | sed 's/.*:\s*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/.*://'

rm test-deployment.yaml
```

## How to Verify in CI

1. **Push a test PR** with problematic files to your fork
2. **Check GitHub Actions** tab to see the security scan job
3. **Verify the job fails** when secrets or unapproved tags are detected
4. **Fix the issues** and push again to confirm the job passes
5. **Review PR comments** for automated notifications when scans fail

## Best Practices

- Store approved image tags in a config file or secret management system
- Use semantic versioning for image tags
- Implement secret management (Kubernetes Secrets, Vault, etc.)
- Regularly update the baseline after auditing
- Enable dependency scanning for container images
- Use image signing and verification for production deployments

## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

```javascript
kind: ClusterPolicy
```
